results.title: Portugal coach Martínez provides fitness update ahead of Nigeria clash
highlights:
Portugal coach Martínez provides fitness update ahead of Nigeria clash

Portugal head coach Roberto Martínez has provided an update on the fitness of key players ahead of his side’s upcoming international fixtures, including their friendly against Nigeria.

Speaking at a press conference, Martínez confirmed that Manchester City right-back Matheus Nunes is currently not fit to train and will miss Portugal’s first warm-up match against Chile.

The Seleção das Quinas are scheduled to face the Super Eagles of Nigeria on Wednesday, June 10, a fixture that coincides with Portugal Day, a national public holiday commemorating poet Luís de Camões.

### Injury concerns shape Portugal’s preparations

Martínez stressed that the coaching staff will avoid rushing players back too soon, particularly with multiple games in close succession.

“Unfortunately, Matheus Nunes is not yet fit to train, so he is out of the squad for tomorrow. It’s not the time to take risks. We hope Matheus will be fit for the second game against Nigeria,” he said, as quoted by A Bola.

The Portugal coach also provided an update on forward João Félix, who remains under observation and will undergo a late fitness assessment before a final decision is made.

“João Félix will train and we will make a decision after training, but I think it’s a different situation. I feel it’s positive and that he will be fit to play tomorrow,” Martínez added.

### Nigeria fixture part of broader preparation plan

Martínez also explained that the timing of the Nigeria match carries symbolic and psychological value as part of Portugal’s World Cup broader preparation.

Meanwhile, the Super Eagles have already begun preparations in Lisbon, with 22 players participating in training sessions on Friday, including winger Samuel Chukwueze, and midfielder Alex Iwobi.

After a long qualifying campaign and extensive scouting, both at club level and in friendly matches, Roberto Martínez has finalized the list. This is the group heading to the World Cup, a tournament that Portuguese fans hope will end in the best possible way: with the national team captain lifting the trophy in the final on July 19. It’s worth noting that Martínez will take 27 players to North America, even though only 26 can be officially registered, including four goalkeepers. Here are Portugal’s 26 + 1 players for the 2026 World Cup: • Goalkeepers: Diogo Costa (FC Porto), Rui Silva (Sporting CP), Ricardo Velho (Gençlerbirliği), José Sá (Wolverhampton) • Defenders: Rúben Dias (Manchester City), Gonçalo Inácio (Sporting CP), João Cancelo (FC Barcelona), Nuno Mendes (PSG), Diogo Dalot (Manchester United), Nélson Semedo (Fenerbahçe SK), Tomás Araújo (Benfica), Renato Veiga (Villarreal) • Midfielders: Vitinha (PSG), João Neves (PSG), Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United), Rúben Neves (Al Hilal), Matheus Nunes (Manchester City), Samú Costa (Mallorca), Bernardo Silva (Manchester City) • Forwards: Cristiano Ronaldo (Al Nassr), Francisco Trincão (Sporting CP), João Félix (Al Nassr), Gonçalo Ramos (PSG), Pedro Neto (Chelsea), Francisco Conceição (Juventus), Rafael Leão (AC Milan), Gonçalo Guedes (Real Sociedad) Note: Ricardo Velho will travel as the 27th player, meaning he will not be on the official FIFA list but will stay with the Portugal national team squad and could be registered if a goalkeeper gets injured during the tournament.
[...]
This squad doesn’t feature the kind of high-profile omissions seen with other nations, like Camavinga and Kolo Muani for France, João Pedro for Brazil, or Carvajal for Spain. Still, there are a few noteworthy surprises. First, the inclusion of four goalkeepers, including Ricardo Velho, stands out. In defense, António Silva missed out, with his Benfica teammate Tomás Araújo taking his place. Midfield is where things get more nuanced. Samú Costa earns a call-up after a strong season with Mallorca, while players like Palhinha, Mateus Fernandes, Pedro Gonçalves (Pote), and especially young talent Rodrigo Mora are left out, for now delaying their debut on the world stage. Up front, Gonçalo Ramos’ inclusion comes as no surprise and Gonçalo Guedes returns to the squad, offering new attacking options. According to Roberto Martínez, he brings important qualities to the frontline.
